```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Keep knitted previews at the same physical width as the exported infographic.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(out.width = paste0(PUB$infographic$width_in, "in"))

# Set TRUE only when you want the QA audit printed in the knitted HTML.
INFOGRAPHIC_AUDIT_SHOW <- FALSE


# ============================================================================
# UNIFORM INFOGRAPHIC PAGE CONTRACT — ALL SIX CHAPTERS
# ============================================================================
#
# Publication pages are fixed-size. Each page may contain up to:
#
#   30 body/stat rows
#    5 visible section headers
#   --------------------------------
#   35 rendered row-equivalents
#
# Pages may contain fewer rows when statistics are switched off. The canvas,
# typography, column widths, row height, and export DPI remain fixed.
#
# If an edit creates a sixth section header inside one page, pagination stops
# with an error rather than silently shrinking the page.
# ============================================================================

INFOGRAPHIC_ROWS_PER_PAGE <- 36L
INFOGRAPHIC_SECTION_HEADERS_PER_PAGE <- 6L
INFOGRAPHIC_RENDERED_ROWS_PER_PAGE <-
  INFOGRAPHIC_ROWS_PER_PAGE +
  INFOGRAPHIC_SECTION_HEADERS_PER_PAGE

INFOGRAPHIC_EXPORT_REGISTRY <- new.env(
  parent = emptyenv()
)


infographic_section_header_count <- function(data) {
  if (nrow(data) == 0L) {
    return(0L)
  }

  if (!"Section" %in% names(data)) {
    stop(
      "Infographic data must contain a `Section` column for fixed pagination.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  section <- as.character(
    data$Section
  )

  if (anyNA(section)) {
    stop(
      "Infographic `Section` contains NA values; page-header counts would be ambiguous.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  if (length(section) == 1L) {
    return(1L)
  }

  as.integer(
    1L +
      sum(
        section[-1] !=
          section[-length(section)]
      )
  )
}


infographic_page_contract <- function(
    page_data,
    page_number,
    total_pages
) {
  body_rows <- nrow(
    page_data
  )

  section_headers <- infographic_section_header_count(
    page_data
  )

  rendered_rows <- body_rows +
    section_headers

  is_final <- page_number ==
    total_pages

  problems <- character()

  if (body_rows > INFOGRAPHIC_ROWS_PER_PAGE) {
    problems <- c(
      problems,
      paste0(
        body_rows,
        " body rows > ",
        INFOGRAPHIC_ROWS_PER_PAGE
      )
    )
  }

  if (
    section_headers >
      INFOGRAPHIC_SECTION_HEADERS_PER_PAGE
  ) {
    problems <- c(
      problems,
      paste0(
        section_headers,
        " section headers > ",
        INFOGRAPHIC_SECTION_HEADERS_PER_PAGE
      )
    )
  }

  if (
    rendered_rows >
      INFOGRAPHIC_RENDERED_ROWS_PER_PAGE
  ) {
    problems <- c(
      problems,
      paste0(
        rendered_rows,
        " rendered row-equivalents > ",
        INFOGRAPHIC_RENDERED_ROWS_PER_PAGE
      )
    )
  }

  list(
    body_rows = body_rows,
    section_headers = section_headers,
    rendered_rows = rendered_rows,
    is_final = is_final,
    problems = problems
  )
}


# Deliberately split by BODY rows first. We do not silently reduce the body-row
# count to compensate for too many headings. Instead, the page contract above
# requires the chapter's visible section structure to fit the common 30 + 5
# publication grid.
paginate_infographic_data <- function(
    data,
    build_page = NULL,
    name = NULL,
    output_dir = PATHS$final_infographics,
    rows_per_page = INFOGRAPHIC_ROWS_PER_PAGE,
    section_headers_per_page = INFOGRAPHIC_SECTION_HEADERS_PER_PAGE
) {
  if (nrow(data) < 1L) {
    stop(
      "The infographic contains no data rows.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  rows_per_page <- as.integer(
    rows_per_page
  )

  section_headers_per_page <- as.integer(
    section_headers_per_page
  )

  if (
    length(rows_per_page) != 1L ||
    !is.finite(rows_per_page) ||
    rows_per_page !=
      INFOGRAPHIC_ROWS_PER_PAGE
  ) {
    stop(
      "`rows_per_page` must equal the publication standard of ",
      INFOGRAPHIC_ROWS_PER_PAGE,
      ".",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  if (
    length(section_headers_per_page) != 1L ||
    !is.finite(section_headers_per_page) ||
    section_headers_per_page !=
      INFOGRAPHIC_SECTION_HEADERS_PER_PAGE
  ) {
    stop(
      "`section_headers_per_page` must equal the publication standard of ",
      INFOGRAPHIC_SECTION_HEADERS_PER_PAGE,
      ".",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  page_id <- ceiling(
    seq_len(
      nrow(data)
    ) /
      rows_per_page
  )

  pages <- split(
    data,
    page_id
  )

  total_pages <- length(
    pages
  )

  for (i in seq_along(pages)) {
    contract <- infographic_page_contract(
      pages[[i]],
      page_number = i,
      total_pages = total_pages
    )

    if (length(contract$problems)) {
      stop(
        "Infographic page-contract failure",
        if (!is.null(name)) paste0(" for `", name, "`") else "",
        ", page ",
        i,
        ": ",
        paste(
          contract$problems,
          collapse = "; "
        ),
        ". Keep each page within 30 body rows + 5 visible section headers; ",
        "do not shrink typography or the canvas.",
        call. = FALSE
      )
    }
  }

  pages
}


mark_infographic_continuation_uniform <- function(
    page_data,
    previous_page = NULL
) {
  if (
    is.null(previous_page) ||
    nrow(previous_page) == 0L ||
    nrow(page_data) == 0L
  ) {
    return(page_data)
  }

  previous_section <- tail(
    as.character(
      previous_page$Section
    ),
    1
  )

  first_section <- as.character(
    page_data$Section[[1]]
  )

  if (
    !identical(
      previous_section,
      first_section
    )
  ) {
    return(page_data)
  }

  page_sections <- as.character(
    page_data$Section
  )

  first_change <- which(
    page_sections !=
      first_section
  )

  continued_rows <- if (
    length(first_change)
  ) {
    seq_len(
      first_change[[1]] -
        1L
    )
  } else {
    seq_len(
      nrow(page_data)
    )
  }

  page_data$Section[
    continued_rows
  ] <- paste0(
    first_section,
    " (cont.)"
  )

  page_data
}


verify_infographic_png_dimensions <- function(
    png_path
) {
  expected_width <- as.integer(
    INFOGRAPHIC_SPEC$output_width_px
  )

  expected_height <- as.integer(
    INFOGRAPHIC_SPEC$output_height_px
  )

  actual_width <- NA_integer_
  actual_height <- NA_integer_
  verification <- "export contract"

  if (
    requireNamespace(
      "magick",
      quietly = TRUE
    )
  ) {
    info <- magick::image_info(
      magick::image_read(
        png_path
      )
    )

    actual_width <- as.integer(
      info$width[[1]]
    )

    actual_height <- as.integer(
      info$height[[1]]
    )

    verification <- "magick"
  } else if (
    requireNamespace(
      "png",
      quietly = TRUE
    )
  ) {
    img <- png::readPNG(
      png_path,
      native = TRUE
    )

    dims <- dim(
      img
    )

    actual_height <- as.integer(
      dims[[1]]
    )

    actual_width <- as.integer(
      dims[[2]]
    )

    verification <- "png"
  }

  if (
    is.finite(actual_width) &&
    is.finite(actual_height) &&
    (
      actual_width != expected_width ||
      actual_height != expected_height
    )
  ) {
    stop(
      "Infographic PNG dimension mismatch for ",
      basename(png_path),
      ": got ",
      actual_width,
      "×",
      actual_height,
      " px; expected ",
      expected_width,
      "×",
      expected_height,
      " px.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  list(
    actual_width_px = actual_width,
    actual_height_px = actual_height,
    expected_width_px = expected_width,
    expected_height_px = expected_height,
    verification = verification
  )
}


# Override the helper's exporter inside this Rmd so every chapter is guaranteed
# to use the same body-row rule, section-header rule, continuation treatment,
# fixed canvas, and output-size validation.
export_paginated_infographic <- function(
    data,
    build_page,
    name,
    output_dir = PATHS$final_infographics,
    rows_per_page = INFOGRAPHIC_ROWS_PER_PAGE,
    section_headers_per_page = INFOGRAPHIC_SECTION_HEADERS_PER_PAGE
) {
  pages <- paginate_infographic_data(
    data = data,
    build_page = build_page,
    name = name,
    output_dir = output_dir,
    rows_per_page = rows_per_page,
    section_headers_per_page = section_headers_per_page
  )

  total_pages <- length(
    pages
  )

  exports <- vector(
    "list",
    total_pages
  )

  registry_rows <- vector(
    "list",
    total_pages
  )

  for (i in seq_along(pages)) {
    page_data <- mark_infographic_continuation_uniform(
      page_data = pages[[i]],
      previous_page = if (
        i > 1L
      ) {
        pages[[i - 1L]]
      } else {
        NULL
      }
    )

    table <- build_page(
      page_data = page_data,
      page_number = i,
      total_pages = total_pages,
      is_last_page = i ==
        total_pages
    )

    page_name <- if (
      total_pages == 1L
    ) {
      name
    } else {
      sprintf(
        "%s_page_%02d",
        name,
        i
      )
    }

    export_result <- export_infographic_page(
      table = table,
      name = page_name,
      output_dir = output_dir
    )

    dimension_check <- verify_infographic_png_dimensions(
      export_result$png_path
    )

    contract <- infographic_page_contract(
      pages[[i]],
      page_number = i,
      total_pages = total_pages
    )

    export_result$body_rows <-
      contract$body_rows

    export_result$section_headers <-
      contract$section_headers

    export_result$rendered_rows <-
      contract$rendered_rows

    exports[[i]] <- export_result

    registry_rows[[i]] <- tibble::tibble(
      Name = name,
      Page = i,
      TotalPages = total_pages,
      BodyRows = contract$body_rows,
      SectionHeaders = contract$section_headers,
      RenderedRows = contract$rendered_rows,
      IsFinalPage = contract$is_final,
      WidthIn = INFOGRAPHIC_SPEC$width_in,
      HeightIn = INFOGRAPHIC_SPEC$height_in,
      ExpectedWidthPx =
        dimension_check$expected_width_px,
      ExpectedHeightPx =
        dimension_check$expected_height_px,
      ActualWidthPx =
        dimension_check$actual_width_px,
      ActualHeightPx =
        dimension_check$actual_height_px,
      DimensionVerification =
        dimension_check$verification,
      PNG = export_result$png_path
    )
  }

  INFOGRAPHIC_EXPORT_REGISTRY[[name]] <-
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      registry_rows
    )

  message(
    "Saved ",
    total_pages,
    " fixed-format page",
    if (total_pages == 1L) "" else "s",
    " for ",
    name,
    ". Page composition: ",
    paste(
      vapply(
        seq_along(pages),
        function(i) {
          contract <- infographic_page_contract(
            pages[[i]],
            page_number = i,
            total_pages = total_pages
          )

          paste0(
            contract$body_rows,
            " body + ",
            contract$section_headers,
            " headers"
          )
        },
        character(1)
      ),
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    ". Canvas = ",
    INFOGRAPHIC_SPEC$width_in,
    " × ",
    INFOGRAPHIC_SPEC$height_in,
    " in."
  )

  exports
}

# CURRENT REPORT SOURCE WHITELIST
# ============================================================================
# The infographic may draw from BOTH:
#   1. source files used by the current figures.Rmd, and
#   2. source files used by the current tables.Rmd.

CURRENT_REPORT_SOURCES <- unique(c(
  CURRENT_FIGURE_SOURCES,
  CURRENT_TABLE_SOURCES
))

read_current_source <- function(id, meta_id = id) {
  if (!id %in% CURRENT_REPORT_SOURCES) {
    stop(
      "`", id, "` is not referenced by the current figures.Rmd or tables.Rmd. ",
      "Update CURRENT_REPORT_SOURCES only after the report source files change.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  read_infographic_source(id, meta_id = meta_id)
}

read_current_figure <- function(id, meta_id = id) {
  if (!id %in% CURRENT_FIGURE_SOURCES) {
    stop("`", id, "` is not a current figure source.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  read_current_source(id, meta_id = meta_id)
}

read_current_table <- function(id, meta_id = id) {
  if (!id %in% CURRENT_TABLE_SOURCES) {
    stop("`", id, "` is not a current table source.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  read_current_source(id, meta_id = meta_id)
}


# ============================================================================
# GENERIC BY-THE-NUMBERS HELPERS
# ============================================================================

info_label <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x) || !nzchar(trimws(as.character(x)))) return("—")
  as.character(x)
}

info_cell <- function(value, label, value_type, projected = FALSE) {
  if (!is.finite(value)) return("—")

  suffix <- if (projected) "P" else ""
  paste0(format_value(value, value_type), " (", info_label(label), suffix, ")")
}

metric_values <- function(
    stat_id,
    section_id,
    section,
    measure,
    first_value,
    first_label,
    last_value,
    last_label,
    value_type,
    change_type,
    emphasis = FALSE,
    projected = FALSE
) {
  tibble(
    StatID   = stat_id,
    SectionID = section_id,
    Section  = section,
    Measure  = measure,
    Earlier  = info_cell(first_value, first_label, value_type),
    Latest   = info_cell(last_value, last_label, value_type, projected = projected),
    Change   = format_change(first_value, last_value, change_type),
    Emphasis = emphasis
  )
}

metric_series <- function(
    stat_id,
    section_id,
    section,
    measure,
    df,
    column,
    value_type,
    change_type,
    year_column = "Year",
    academic = FALSE,
    emphasis = FALSE,
    transform = identity
) {
  first <- data_endpoint(
    df,
    column,
    which = "first",
    year_column = year_column,
    academic = academic
  )

  last <- data_endpoint(
    df,
    column,
    which = "last",
    year_column = year_column,
    academic = academic
  )

  first$value <- transform(first$value)
  last$value  <- transform(last$value)

  metric_values(
    stat_id = stat_id,
    section_id = section_id,
    section = section,
    measure = measure,
    first_value = first$value,
    first_label = first$label,
    last_value = last$value,
    last_label = last$label,
    value_type = value_type,
    change_type = change_type,
    emphasis = emphasis
  )
}

metric_snapshot <- function(
    stat_id,
    section_id,
    section,
    measure,
    value,
    label,
    value_type,
    emphasis = FALSE
) {
  tibble(
    StatID    = stat_id,
    SectionID = section_id,
    Section   = section,
    Measure   = measure,
    Earlier   = "—",
    Latest    = info_cell(value, label, value_type),
    Change    = "—",
    Emphasis  = emphasis
  )
}

metric_text <- function(
    stat_id,
    section_id,
    section,
    measure,
    earlier,
    latest,
    change = "—",
    emphasis = FALSE
) {
  tibble(
    StatID    = stat_id,
    SectionID = section_id,
    Section   = section,
    Measure   = measure,
    Earlier   = earlier,
    Latest    = latest,
    Change    = change,
    Emphasis  = emphasis
  )
}

latest_row <- function(df, year_column = "Year") {
  yr <- year_number(df[[year_column]])
  df[which.max(yr), , drop = FALSE]
}

first_last_year_labels <- function(df, year_column = "Year") {
  yrs <- year_number(df[[year_column]])
  yrs <- yrs[is.finite(yrs)]
  c(first = as.character(min(yrs)), last = as.character(max(yrs)))
}

finalize_infographic_data <- function(data, section_order) {
  data %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data$Measure), nzchar(.data$Measure)) %>%
    mutate(
      Section = factor(.data$Section, levels = section_order),
      RowOrder = row_number()
    ) %>%
    arrange(.data$Section, .data$RowOrder)
}


# ============================================================================
# EDITORIAL LABEL CLEANUP
# ============================================================================
# Keep the section header responsible for the repeated concept ("international",
# "temporary visa holder share", "US universities in the global top 100", etc.)
# and keep individual measure labels short enough to scan in one line.

editorialize_infographic_data <- function(data, chapter_number) {
  out <- data %>%
    mutate(
      Section = as.character(.data$Section),
      Measure = as.character(.data$Measure)
    )

  if (chapter_number == 2) {
    out <- out %>%
      mutate(
        Section = recode(
          .data$Section,
          "Where international students come from" = "Countries of origin",
          "Where international students concentrate" = "Fields and STEM concentration"
        ),

        Measure = case_when(
          .data$SectionID == "origin" ~
            str_replace(.data$Measure, " share of international ", " — "),

          .data$StatID == "tab201_asia_count" ~ "Students from Asia",
          .data$StatID == "tab201_asia_share" ~ "Asia share",
          .data$StatID == "tab201_europe_share" ~ "Europe share",
          .data$StatID == "tab201_subsaharan_share" ~ "Sub-Saharan Africa share",

          .data$SectionID == "field" &
            str_detect(.data$Measure, "^International students in ") ~
            str_remove(.data$Measure, "^International students in "),

          .data$SectionID == "field" &
            str_detect(.data$Measure, "^International STEM students from ") ~
            str_replace(
              .data$Measure,
              "^International STEM students from ",
              "STEM students from "
            ),

          .data$StatID == "economic_contribution" ~
            "Contribution to the US economy",

          .data$Measure == "Institutions citing visa application process" ~
            "Visa application process",

          .data$Measure == "Institutions citing u.s. travel restrictions" ~
            "US travel restrictions",

          .data$Measure == "Institutions citing feeling unwelcome in the united states" ~
            "Feeling unwelcome in the US",

          .data$Measure == "Institutions citing social and political environment in the united states" ~
            "US social and political environment",

          TRUE ~ .data$Measure
        )
      )
  }

  if (chapter_number == 3) {
    out <- out %>%
      mutate(
        Section = recode(
          .data$Section,
          "International talent in the education-to-work pipeline" =
            "Education-to-work pipeline",
          "Which STEM graduates work in STEM" =
            "STEM graduates working in STEM",
          "Where temporary visa holders concentrate" =
            "Temporary-visa-holder share by occupation"
        ),

        Measure = case_when(
          .data$StatID == "pipeline_masters" ~ "Master’s students",
          .data$StatID == "pipeline_doctorate" ~ "Doctorate students",
          .data$StatID == "pipeline_opt" ~ "Optional Practical Training",

          .data$StatID == "postdoc_science" ~ "Share of science postdocs",
          .data$StatID == "postdoc_engineering" ~ "Share of engineering postdocs",
          .data$StatID == "postdoc_health" ~ "Share of health postdocs",

          .data$StatID == "stem_conversion_us" ~
            "US-born doctorate holders in STEM",
          .data$StatID == "stem_conversion_foreign" ~
            "Foreign-born doctorate holders in STEM",

          .data$SectionID == "degree_work" ~
            str_remove(.data$Measure, " employed in STEM occupations$"),

          .data$SectionID == "visa_concentration" ~
            str_remove(.data$Measure, "^Temporary-visa-holder share: "),

          .data$StatID == "ai_all_foreign" ~
            "All-foreign-born founder teams",
          .data$StatID == "ai_some_foreign" ~
            "Some foreign-born founders",
          .data$StatID == "founder_origin_1" ~
            "Largest immigrant-founder origin",

          TRUE ~ .data$Measure
        )
      )
  }

  if (chapter_number == 4) {
    # Remove the redundant 2022 PISA-math snapshot because the time-series row
    # immediately above already ends at the same 2022 value.
    out <- out %>%
      filter(.data$StatID != "us_oecd_math") %>%
      mutate(
        Section = recode(
          .data$Section,
          "Keeping STEM students in STEM" = "STEM persistence by field",
          "What Americans study abroad" = "Fields studied abroad",
          "Where Americans study abroad" = "Destinations abroad"
        ),

        Measure = case_when(
          .data$StatID == "us_math_gap" ~ "PISA math vs OECD average",
          .data$StatID == "us_science_gap" ~ "PISA science vs OECD average",
          .data$StatID == "us_reading_gap" ~ "PISA reading vs OECD average",
          .data$StatID == "us_top_math" ~ "Students at PISA math Levels 5–6",

          .data$StatID == "us_k12_spending" ~
            "K–12 spending and PISA math score",
          .data$StatID == "us_spending_ratio" ~
            "Tertiary-to-K–12 spending ratio",

          .data$StatID == "early_exit" ~
            "Left without return in first two years",

          .data$SectionID == "persistence" ~
            str_remove(.data$Measure, ": graduates remaining in entry field$"),

          .data$StatID == "tab401_stem_bachelors" ~
            "Completed a STEM bachelor’s degree",
          .data$StatID == "tab401_nonstem_bachelors" ~
            "Completed a non-STEM bachelor’s degree",
          .data$StatID == "tab401_left_no_degree" ~
            "Left with no degree",

          .data$StatID == "tab402_never" ~ "Never switched majors",
          .data$StatID == "tab402_multiple" ~
            "Switched majors more than once",

          .data$SectionID == "study_abroad" ~
            str_remove(.data$Measure, "^US study-abroad students in "),

          .data$SectionID == "study_abroad_region" ~
            str_remove(.data$Measure, "^US study-abroad students going to "),

          .data$StatID == "outbound_us" ~
            "United States — tertiary students studying abroad",
          .data$StatID == "outbound_china" ~
            "China — tertiary students studying abroad",
          .data$StatID == "outbound_india" ~
            "India — tertiary students studying abroad",
          .data$StatID == "netflow_us" ~
            "United States — net student flow (millions)",
          .data$StatID == "netflow_china" ~
            "China — net student flow (millions)",

          TRUE ~ .data$Measure
        )
      )
  }

  if (chapter_number == 5) {
    out <- out %>%
      mutate(
        Section = recode(
          .data$Section,
          "The institutional bench" =
            "US universities in the global top 100",
          "Patent leadership is shifting" = "Patent leadership"
        ),

        Measure = case_when(
          .data$StatID == "neurips_us" ~
            "US — NeurIPS oral-presentation authors",
          .data$StatID == "neurips_cn" ~
            "China — NeurIPS oral-presentation authors",
          .data$StatID == "topcited_us" ~
            "US — top-cited emerging-tech publications",
          .data$StatID == "topcited_cn" ~
            "China — top-cited emerging-tech publications",
          .data$StatID == "topauthors_us" ~
            "Top papers — US author",
          .data$StatID == "topauthors_cn" ~
            "Top papers — China-based author",
          .data$StatID == "researchers_us" ~
            "Top-1% most-cited researchers — US",
          .data$StatID == "researchers_cn" ~
            "Top-1% most-cited researchers — China",

          .data$StatID == "tab501_conference_us" ~ "Median US share",
          .data$StatID == "tab501_conference_china" ~ "Median China share",
          .data$StatID == "tab501_china_leads" ~
            "Conferences where China leads the US",

          .data$SectionID == "institutional" ~
            str_remove(
              .data$Measure,
              "^US universities in the global top 100: "
            ),

          .data$StatID == "rd_spend_us" ~
            "US spending (billions, 2020 PPP)",
          .data$StatID == "rd_spend_cn" ~
            "China spending (billions, 2020 PPP)",
          .data$StatID == "rd_intensity_us" ~ "US intensity",
          .data$StatID == "rd_intensity_cn" ~ "China intensity",

          .data$StatID == "basic_us" ~ "US basic research",
          .data$StatID == "basic_cn" ~ "China basic research",
          .data$StatID == "business_us" ~ "US business-sector R&D",
          .data$StatID == "business_cn" ~ "China business-sector R&D",

          .data$SectionID == "patents" &
            str_detect(.data$Measure, "^US–China patent-grant gap: ") ~
            str_replace(
              .data$Measure,
              "^US–China patent-grant gap: ",
              "US–China grant gap: "
            ),

          .data$SectionID == "patents" &
            str_detect(.data$Measure, " US patent grants$") ~
            paste(
              str_remove(.data$Measure, " US patent grants$"),
              "patent grants"
            ),

          TRUE ~ .data$Measure
        )
      )
  }

  if (chapter_number == 6) {
    out <- out %>%
      mutate(
        Section = recode(
          .data$Section,
          "Stay intentions by region of origin" = "Stay intentions by region",
          "Employment-based green-card wait times" =
            "Employment-based green-card waits"
        ),

        Measure = case_when(
          .data$StatID == "intend_stay" ~
            "PhD recipients intending to stay in the US",

          .data$SectionID == "regional_stay" ~
            str_replace(
              .data$Measure,
              "^(.+): international STEM PhDs intending to stay in the US$",
              "\\1"
            ),

          .data$StatID == "tab602_computing" ~
            "Computer and information sciences PhDs",
          .data$StatID == "tab602_engineering" ~ "Engineering PhDs",

          .data$StatID == "tab603_tvh_academe" ~
            "Temporary visa holders — academe",
          .data$StatID == "tab603_tvh_industry" ~
            "Temporary visa holders — industry/business",
          .data$StatID == "tab603_us_industry" ~
            "US citizens — industry/business",

          .data$SectionID == "perm" ~
            str_replace(
              .data$Measure,
              "^(.+): share of PERM certifications expiring unused$",
              "\\1"
            ),

          .data$StatID == "workforce_gap_us" ~
            "US immigrant workforce-participation gap",

          .data$StatID == "trained_total" ~
            "STEM doctorate recipients in cohort",
          .data$StatID == "trained_left" ~
            "Estimated no longer in the US after ~10 years",
          .data$StatID == "training_value_left" ~
            "Estimated US training investment that left",

          TRUE ~ .data$Measure
        )
      )
  }

  out
}


export_current_chapter <- function(
    data,
    chapter_number,
    title,
    subtitle,
    name,
    source_figures,
    section_order,
    note_text = NULL,
    column_labels = c(
      Earlier = "Earlier<br>value",
      Latest = "Latest or<br>Projected Value",
      Change = "Change"
    ),
    trend_right_padding_px = 0,
    show_header = TRUE,
    rows_per_page = INFOGRAPHIC_ROWS_PER_PAGE
) {
  data <- finalize_infographic_data(
    data,
    section_order
  ) %>%
    editorialize_infographic_data(chapter_number)

  build_page <- function(
      page_data,
      page_number,
      total_pages,
      is_last_page
  ) {
    final_notes <- character()

    if (is_last_page) {
      if (!is.null(note_text) && length(note_text)) {
        final_notes <- c(
          final_notes,
          note_text
        )
      }

      final_notes <- c(
        final_notes,
        paste0(
          "**Source:** Derived from the current report figures and tables: ",
          paste(source_figures, collapse = ", "),
          ". See the cited figures and tables for full source information."
        )
      )
    }

    build_infographic_table(
      data = page_data,
      id = paste0(name, "_page_", page_number),
      chapter_number = chapter_number,
      title = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      column_labels = column_labels,
      notes = final_notes,
      layout = INFOGRAPHIC_FIXED_LAYOUT,
      trend_right_padding_px = trend_right_padding_px,
      row_padding_px = INFOGRAPHIC_FIXED_LAYOUT$row_padding_px,
      nowrap_values = TRUE,
      show_header = show_header
    )
  }

  exports <- export_paginated_infographic(
    data = data,
    build_page = build_page,
    name = name,
    rows_per_page = rows_per_page
  )

  knitr::include_graphics(
    vapply(
      exports,
      `[[`,
      character(1),
      "png_path"
    )
  )
}
```

# Chapter 1

```{r infographic_ch1_by_the_numbers, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# ============================================================================
# CHAPTER 1: AMERICA'S STEM TALENT SYSTEM — BY THE NUMBERS
#
# Comparison convention:
#   - Historical column = 1995 for all current/historical measures.
#   - *  = source series contains usable data before 1995.
#   - Current column = 2025 where available.
#   - ** = latest usable observation is 2024 rather than 2025.
#   - Projection rows remain optional and are off by default.
#
# Current report sources:
#   Figures 1.01–1.08 and Table 1.01.
# ============================================================================


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. INCLUDE / EXCLUDE CONTROLS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Set any statistic to FALSE to remove it. Filtering happens before pagination,
# so the figure automatically adjusts to the included rows.

CH1_INCLUDE <- c(

  # Expansion of US higher education
  research_doctorates = TRUE,
  all_bachelors = TRUE,
  all_masters = TRUE,
  all_doctorates = TRUE,

  # Growth and composition of STEM training
  stem_total = TRUE,
  stem_bachelors = TRUE,
  stem_masters = TRUE,
  stem_doctorates = TRUE,
  stem_md_ratio = TRUE,
  stem_share_bachelors = TRUE,
  stem_share_masters = TRUE,
  stem_share_doctorates = TRUE,

  # International enrollment and degree dependence
  intl_students = TRUE,
  intl_enrollment_share = TRUE,
  intl_all_bachelors = TRUE,
  intl_all_masters = TRUE,
  intl_all_doctorates = TRUE,
  intl_stem_bachelors = TRUE,
  intl_stem_masters = TRUE,
  intl_stem_doctorates = TRUE,

  # Table 1.01 selected fields
  tab101_cs_bachelors = TRUE,
  tab101_engineering_bachelors = TRUE,
  tab101_math_bachelors = TRUE,
  tab101_physical_sciences_bachelors = TRUE,

  tab101_cs_masters = TRUE,
  tab101_engineering_masters = TRUE,
  tab101_math_masters = TRUE,
  tab101_physical_sciences_masters = TRUE,

  tab101_cs_doctorates = TRUE,
  tab101_engineering_doctorates = TRUE,
  tab101_math_doctorates = TRUE,
  tab101_physical_sciences_doctorates = TRUE,

  # Projections — off by default
  proj_us_total = FALSE,
  proj_china_total = FALSE,
  proj_india_total = FALSE,
  proj_us_percap = FALSE,
  proj_china_percap = FALSE,
  proj_india_percap = FALSE
)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# COMPARISON-YEAR RULES
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# These are publication comparison rules, not inferred source endpoints.

CH1_BASELINE_YEAR <- 1995L
CH1_TARGET_YEAR <- 2025L
CH1_FALLBACK_YEAR <- 2024L


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. CURRENT REPORT SOURCES
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fig101 <- read_current_figure("FIG101") %>%
  select(
    Year,
    value = 2
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      everything(),
      as.numeric
    )
  )


fig102 <- read_current_figure("FIG102")

fig103 <- read_current_figure("FIG103")


fig104 <- read_current_figure("FIG104") %>%

    Year = 1,

    Share = 3
  ) %>%

    )

fig105 <- read_current_figure("FIG105")

fig106 <- read_current_figure("FIG106")


fig107_long <- read_current_figure("FIG107") %>%
  pivot_observed_projected()


fig108_long <- read_current_figure("FIG108") %>%
  pivot_observed_projected()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# TABLE 1.01 — LONG-FORMAT SOURCE
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Expected columns:
#   Year
#   Field
#   Degree
#   Nonresident_Total
#   Grand_Total
#   NonresidentShare
#
# The two engineering source categories are collapsed to "Engineering" by
# summing underlying counts and recomputing the share.

tab101_long <- prepare_tab101_data(
  "TAB101"
)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. COMPARISON-ENDPOINT HELPERS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


# 1995 baseline.
#
# The displayed value always comes from 1995.
# has_earlier_history records whether usable observations exist before 1995.

ch1_baseline_endpoint <- function(
    df,
    column,
    year_column = "Year",
    academic = FALSE
) {

  series <- series_data(
    df,
    column,
    year_column
  )


  baseline <- series %>%
    filter(
      .data$Year ==
        CH1_BASELINE_YEAR
    ) %>%
    slice_head(
      n = 1
    )


  if (
    nrow(
      baseline
    ) != 1L
  ) {

    stop(
      "Chapter 1 requires a usable ",
      CH1_BASELINE_YEAR,
      " observation for `",
      column,
      "`.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }


  list(

    value =
      baseline$Value[[1]],

    year =
      CH1_BASELINE_YEAR,

    has_earlier_history =
      any(
        series$Year <
          CH1_BASELINE_YEAR
      ),

    label = if (
      academic
    ) {
      academic_period_label(
        df,
        CH1_BASELINE_YEAR
      )
    } else {
      calendar_year_label(
        CH1_BASELINE_YEAR
      )
    }
  )
}


# Current endpoint.
#
# Use 2025 where available; otherwise use 2024.

ch1_current_endpoint <- function(
    df,
    column,
    year_column = "Year",
    academic = FALSE
) {

  series <- series_data(
    df,
    column,
    year_column
  )


  preferred_years <- c(
    CH1_TARGET_YEAR,
    CH1_FALLBACK_YEAR
  )


  chosen_year <- preferred_years[
    preferred_years %in%
      series$Year
  ]


  if (
    !length(
      chosen_year
    )
  ) {

    stop(
      "Chapter 1 requires a ",
      CH1_TARGET_YEAR,
      " value, or a ",
      CH1_FALLBACK_YEAR,
      " fallback, for `",
      column,
      "`.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }


  chosen_year <- chosen_year[[1]]


  row <- series %>%
    filter(
      .data$Year ==
        .env$chosen_year
    ) %>%
    slice_head(
      n = 1
    )


  list(

    value =
      row$Value[[1]],

    year =
      chosen_year,

    label = if (
      academic
    ) {
      academic_period_label(
        df,
        chosen_year
      )
    } else {
      calendar_year_label(
        chosen_year
      )
    }
  )
}


# Generic Chapter 1 metric helper.
#
# Display convention:
#   1995 column:
#     value*
#     if source data extend before 1995
#
#   2025 column:
#     value
#     if 2025 exists
#
#     value**
#     if 2024 is used instead

ch1_metric_series <- function(
    stat_id,
    section_id,
    section,
    measure,
    df,
    column,
    value_type,
    change_type,
    year_column = "Year",
    academic = FALSE,
    emphasis = FALSE,
    transform = identity
) {

  first <- ch1_baseline_endpoint(
    df,
    column,
    year_column = year_column,
    academic = academic
  )


  last <- ch1_current_endpoint(
    df,
    column,
    year_column = year_column,
    academic = academic
  )


  first$value <- transform(
    first$value
  )


  last$value <- transform(
    last$value
  )


  out <- metric_values(

    stat_id =
      stat_id,

    section_id =
      section_id,

    section =
      section,

    measure =
      measure,

    first_value =
      first$value,

    first_label =
      first$label,

    last_value =
      last$value,

    last_label =
      last$label,

    value_type =
      value_type,

    change_type =
      change_type,

    emphasis =
      emphasis
  )


  # Column header already says 1995.
  out$Earlier <- paste0(

    format_value(
      first$value,
      value_type
    ),

    if (
      first$has_earlier_history
    ) {
      "*"
    } else {
      ""
    }
  )


  # Column header already says 2025.
  out$Latest <- paste0(

    format_value(
      last$value,
      value_type
    ),

    if (
      identical(
        as.integer(
          last$year
        ),
        CH1_FALLBACK_YEAR
      )
    ) {
      "**"
    } else {
      ""
    }
  )


  out
}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. DERIVED STEM COMPOSITION MEASURES
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fig102_degree_totals <- fig102 %>%

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. TABLE 1.01 FIELD-SHARE HELPER
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Uses the same 1995 / 2025 comparison convention as every other current
# Chapter 1 statistic.
#
# Engineering has already been combined in tab101_long from underlying counts.

field_share_metric <- function(
    field,
    degree,
    measure,
    stat_id,
    emphasis = FALSE
) {

  series <- tab101_long %>%

    filter(

      normalize_label(
        .data$Field
      ) ==
        normalize_label(
          .env$field
        ),

      .data$Degree ==
        .env$degree,

      is.finite(
        .data$NonresidentShare
      )
    ) %>%

    arrange(
      .data$Year
    )


  if (
    nrow(
      series
    ) == 0L
  ) {

    stop(
      "No usable Table 1.01 observations were found for `",
      field,
      "` / `",
      degree,
      "`.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 1995 baseline
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  first <- series %>%

    filter(
      .data$Year ==
        CH1_BASELINE_YEAR
    ) %>%

    slice_head(
      n = 1
    )


  if (
    nrow(
      first
    ) != 1L
  ) {

    stop(
      "Table 1.01 requires a usable ",
      CH1_BASELINE_YEAR,
      " observation for `",
      field,
      "` / `",
      degree,
      "`.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }


  has_earlier_history <- any(
    series$Year <
      CH1_BASELINE_YEAR
  )


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 2025 current value, with 2024 fallback
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  preferred_years <- c(
    CH1_TARGET_YEAR,
    CH1_FALLBACK_YEAR
  )


  available_current_years <- preferred_years[
    preferred_years %in%
      series$Year
  ]


  if (
    !length(
      available_current_years
    )
  ) {

    stop(
      "Table 1.01 has neither a ",
      CH1_TARGET_YEAR,
      " nor ",
      CH1_FALLBACK_YEAR,
      " usable observation for `",
      field,
      "` / `",
      degree,
      "`.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }


  current_year <-
    available_current_years[[1]]


  last <- series %>%

    filter(
      .data$Year ==
        .env$current_year
    ) %>%

    slice_head(
      n = 1
    )


  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Build infographic row
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  out <- metric_values(

    stat_id =
      stat_id,

    section_id =
      "field_dependence",

    section =
      "International share in selected STEM fields",

    measure =
      measure,

    first_value =
      first$NonresidentShare[[1]],

    first_label =
      CH1_BASELINE_YEAR,

    last_value =
      last$NonresidentShare[[1]],

    last_label =
      last$Year[[1]],

    value_type =
      "percent_value",

    change_type =
      "pp_percent",

    emphasis =
      emphasis
  )


  out$Earlier <- paste0(

    format_value(
      first$NonresidentShare[[1]],
      "percent_value"
    ),

    if (
      has_earlier_history
    ) {
      "*"
    } else {
      ""
    }
  )


  out$Latest <- paste0(

    format_value(
      last$NonresidentShare[[1]],
      "percent_value"
    ),

    if (
      identical(
        as.integer(
          last$Year[[1]]
        ),
        CH1_FALLBACK_YEAR
      )
    ) {
      "**"
    } else {
      ""
    }
  )


  out
}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. PROJECTION HELPER
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

projection_metric <- function(
    df,
    country,
    measure,
    stat_id,
    value_type = "count",
    emphasis = FALSE
) {

  country_df <- df %>%

    filter(

      .data$Country ==
        .env$country,

      is.finite(
        .data$value
      )
    )


  observed <- country_df %>%

    filter(
      .data$period ==
        "Observed"
    ) %>%

    arrange(
      .data$Year
    ) %>%

    slice_tail(
      n = 1
    )


  projected <- country_df %>%

    filter(
      .data$period ==
        "Projected"
    ) %>%

    arrange(
      .data$Year
    ) %>%

    slice_tail(
      n = 1
    )


  if (
    nrow(observed) != 1L ||
      nrow(projected) != 1L
  ) {
    return(
      NULL
    )
  }


  metric_values(

    stat_id =
      stat_id,

    section_id =
      "projection",

    section =
      "Global STEM PhD projections",

    measure =
      measure,

    first_value =
      observed$value[[1]],

    first_label =
      observed$Year[[1]],

    last_value =
      projected$value[[1]],

    last_label =
      projected$Year[[1]],

    value_type =
      value_type,

    change_type =
      "percent",

    emphasis =
      emphasis,

    projected =
      TRUE
  )
}

  "International enrollment and degree dependence",
  "International share in selected STEM fields",
  "Global STEM PhD projections"
)

  ch1_data$SectionID ==
    "projection"
)


# A single * in the 1995 column means that the source series extends further
# back than the selected 1995 comparison year.

ch1_has_prebaseline_history <- any(
  stringr::str_detect(
    ch1_data$Earlier,
    "(?<!\\*)\\*$"
  )
)


# A double ** in the 2025 column means that the latest available observation
# is 2024 rather than 2025.

ch1_has_2024_fallback <- any(
  stringr::str_detect(
    ch1_data$Latest,
    "\\*\\*$"
  )
)


# Default historical/current view:
#
#       MEASURE | 1995 | 2025 | CHANGE
#
# If projection rows are manually enabled, use broader labels because those
# rows compare their latest observed and projected endpoints rather than
# 1995 and 2025.

ch1_column_labels <- c(

  Earlier = if (
    ch1_has_projections
  ) {
    "1995 / Observed"
  } else {
    as.character(
      CH1_BASELINE_YEAR
    )
  },


  Latest = if (
    ch1_has_projections
  ) {
    "2025 / Projected"
  } else {
    as.character(
      CH1_TARGET_YEAR
    )
  },


  Change =
    "Change"
)


ch1_note_text <- c(

  if (
    ch1_has_prebaseline_history
  ) {

    paste0(
      "\\* Data are available further back than ",
      CH1_BASELINE_YEAR,
      " for marked series."
    )

  } else {

    NULL
  },


  if (
    ch1_has_2024_fallback
  ) {

    paste0(
      "\\*\\* Latest data are available through ",
      CH1_FALLBACK_YEAR,
      " for marked series."
    )

  } else {

    NULL
  },


  paste0(

    "**Note:** Historical comparisons use ",
    CH1_BASELINE_YEAR,
    " and ",
    CH1_TARGET_YEAR,
    " observations. ",

    if (
      ch1_has_projections
    ) {

      paste0(
        "Projection rows compare the latest observed year with the latest ",
        "projected year; a “P” marks projections. "
      )

    } else {

      ""
    },

    "Arrow colors indicate direction of change only."
  )
)


export_current_chapter(

  data =
    ch1_data,

  chapter_number =
    1,

  title =
    "AMERICA’S STEM TALENT SYSTEM: BY THE NUMBERS",

  subtitle = if (
    ch1_has_projections
  ) {
    "Historical, current, and projected measures"
  } else {
    "Historical and current measures"
  },

  name =
    "infographic_ch1_by_the_numbers",

  source_figures = c(
    "Figures 1.01–1.08",
    "Table 1.01"
  ),

  section_order =
    ch1_section_order,

  note_text =
    ch1_note_text,

  column_labels =
    ch1_column_labels,

  trend_right_padding_px =
    5,
  
  show_header = FALSE,
)
```

```{r infographic_ch2_by_the_numbers, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. STANDARD 2001 / 2025 ENDPOINT HELPERS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

ch2_baseline_endpoint <- function(
    df,
    column,
    year_column = "Year",
    academic = FALSE,
    allow_earliest_fallback = FALSE
) {

  series <- series_data(
    df,
    column,
    year_column
  )


  baseline <- series %>%
    filter(
      .data$Year ==
        CH2_BASELINE_YEAR
    ) %>%
    slice_head(
      n = 1
    )


  used_fallback <- FALSE


  if (
    nrow(baseline) != 1L
  ) {

    if (
      !isTRUE(
        allow_earliest_fallback
      )
    ) {

      stop(
        "Chapter 2 requires a usable ",
        CH2_BASELINE_YEAR,
        " observation for `",
        column,
        "`.",
        call. = FALSE
      )
    }


    baseline <- series %>%
      slice_head(
        n = 1
      )


    used_fallback <- TRUE
  }


  list(
    value =
      baseline$Value[[1]],

    year =
      baseline$Year[[1]],

    used_fallback =
      used_fallback,

    label = if (
      academic
    ) {
      academic_period_label(
        df,
        baseline$Year[[1]]
      )
    } else {
      calendar_year_label(
        baseline$Year[[1]]
      )
    }
  )
}


ch2_current_endpoint <- function(
    df,
    column,
    year_column = "Year",
    academic = FALSE
) {

  series <- series_data(
    df,
    column,
    year_column
  )


  current <- series %>%
    filter(
      .data$Year ==
        CH2_TARGET_YEAR
    ) %>%
    slice_head(
      n = 1
    )


  if (
    nrow(current) != 1L
  ) {

    stop(
      "Chapter 2 requires a usable ",
      CH2_TARGET_YEAR,
      " observation for `",
      column,
      "`.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }


  list(
    value =
      current$Value[[1]],

    year =
      CH2_TARGET_YEAR,

    label = if (
      academic
    ) {
      academic_period_label(
        df,
        CH2_TARGET_YEAR
      )
    } else {
      calendar_year_label(
        CH2_TARGET_YEAR
      )
    }
  )
}


ch2_metric_series <- function(
    stat_id,
    section_id,
    section,
    measure,
    df,
    column,
    value_type,
    change_type,
    year_column = "Year",
    academic = FALSE,
    emphasis = FALSE,
    transform = identity,
    allow_earliest_fallback = FALSE
) {

  first <- ch2_baseline_endpoint(
    df,
    column,
    year_column = year_column,
    academic = academic,
    allow_earliest_fallback =
      allow_earliest_fallback
  )


  last <- ch2_current_endpoint(
    df,
    column,
    year_column = year_column,
    academic = academic
  )


  first$value <- transform(
    first$value
  )


  last$value <- transform(
    last$value
  )


  out <- metric_values(
    stat_id = stat_id,
    section_id = section_id,
    section = section,
    measure = measure,

    first_value = first$value,
    first_label = first$label,

    last_value = last$value,
    last_label = last$label,

    value_type = value_type,
    change_type = change_type,
    emphasis = emphasis
  )


  # Column header already says 2001.
  out$Earlier <- paste0(
    format_value(
      first$value,
      value_type
    ),

    if (
      first$used_fallback
    ) {
      "*"
    } else {
      ""
    }
  )


  # Column header already says 2025.
  out$Latest <- format_value(
    last$value,
    value_type
  )


  out
}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. REGION-SHARE HELPER
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

ch2_region_share_metric <- function(
    region_column,
    measure,
    stat_id,
    emphasis = FALSE
) {

  region_columns <- setdiff(
    names(ch2_tab201),
    c(
      "Year",
      "Percent Asia"
    )
  )


  tmp <- ch2_tab201 %>%
    mutate(
      Year =
        year_number(.data$Year),

      across(
        -Year,
        numeric_clean
      ),

      Total = rowSums(
        across(
          all_of(region_columns)
        ),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

      Value =
        .data[[region_column]] /
        .data$Total
    ) %>%
    filter(
      is.finite(.data$Year),
      is.finite(.data$Value)
    )


  ch2_metric_series(
    stat_id = stat_id,
    section_id = "geography",
    section = "Geographic concentration",
    measure = measure,
    df = tmp,
    column = "Value",
    value_type = "share",
    change_type = "pp_share",
    emphasis = emphasis
  )
}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. FIG206 — DIRECT 2025 ACTUAL / 2026 PROJECTION
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

ch2_projection_metric <- function(
    category,
    stat_id,
    measure,
    emphasis = FALSE
) {

  row <- ch2_fig206 %>%
    filter(
      normalize_label(.data$Category) ==
        normalize_label(.env$category)
    )


  if (
    nrow(row) != 1L
  ) {

    stop(
      "Expected exactly one FIG206 row for `",
      category,
      "`.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }


  first_value <-
    row[["2025"]][[1]]

  last_value <-
    row[["2026"]][[1]]

  reported_change <-
    row$Change[[1]]


  if (
    !is.finite(first_value) ||
      !is.finite(last_value) ||
      !is.finite(reported_change)
  ) {

    stop(
      "FIG206 contains an unusable 2025, 2026, or Change value for `",
      category,
      "`.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }


  out <- metric_values(
    stat_id = stat_id,

    section_id =
      "projected_enrollment",

    section =
      "Projected Changes to International Enrollment Between 2025 and 2026",

    measure =
      measure,

    first_value =
      first_value,

    first_label =
      2025,

    last_value =
      last_value,

    last_label =
      2026,

    value_type =
      "count",

    change_type =
      "percent",

    emphasis =
      emphasis,

    projected =
      TRUE
  )


  # * = left-column value is 2025 actual rather than 2001.
  out$Earlier <- paste0(
    format_value(
      first_value,
      "count"
    ),
    "*"
  )


  # Small P = 2026 projection.
  out$Latest <- paste0(
    format_value(
      last_value,
      "count"
    ),
    "ᴾ"
  )


  # Use FIG206's reported change directly.
  out$Change <- paste0(
    if (
      reported_change > 0
    ) {
      "+"
    } else {
      ""
    },

    scales::number(
      reported_change,
      accuracy = 1
    ),

    "%"
  )


  out
}

ch2_slug <- function(x) {

  x %>%
    stringr::str_to_lower() %>%
    stringr::str_replace_all(
      "[^a-z0-9]+",
      "_"
    ) %>%
    stringr::str_remove(
      "^_"
    ) %>%
    stringr::str_remove(
      "_$"
    )
}


# 2025 endpoint from updated FIG207new.

ch2_recruitment_2025 <- ch2_fig207new_long %>%
  filter(
    .data$Year ==
      2025L
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    Priority =
      as.character(.data$Priority),

    Value2025 =
      .data$Percent
  )


# Like-for-like country comparisons only.

ch2_recruitment_changes <- CH2_RECRUITMENT_2015_ALL %>%
  filter(
    .data$Priority %in%
      CH2_RECRUITMENT_COUNTRIES
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    Priority =
      as.character(.data$Priority),

    Value2015 =
      .data$Percent
  ) %>%
  inner_join(
    ch2_recruitment_2025,
    by = "Priority"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Change =
      .data$Value2025 -
      .data$Value2015,

    StatID = paste0(
      "recruitment_",
      ch2_slug(
        .data$Priority
      )
    )
  )


# Three countries with the largest absolute changes.

ch2_recruitment_top3 <- ch2_recruitment_changes %>%
  arrange(
    desc(
      abs(.data$Change)
    ),
    .data$Priority
  ) %>%
  slice_head(
    n = 3
  )


ch2_recruitment_top3_stats <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  ch2_recruitment_top3,

  function(
      Priority,
      Value2015,
      Value2025,
      Change,
      StatID,
      ...
  ) {

    out <- metric_values(
      stat_id =
        StatID,

      section_id =
        "recruitment",

      section =
        "Recruitment and barriers (2015–2025)",

      measure = paste0(
        "Institutions citing ",
        Priority,
        " as a recruitment priority"
      ),

      first_value =
        Value2015,

      first_label =
        2015,

      last_value =
        Value2025,

      last_label =
        2025,

      value_type =
        "percent_value",

      change_type =
        "pp_percent"
    )


    # * = left-column value is 2015 rather than 2001.
    out$Earlier <- paste0(
      format_value(
        Value2015,
        "percent_value"
      ),
      "*"
    )


    out$Latest <- format_value(
      Value2025,
      "percent_value"
    )


    out
  }
)

ch2_barrier_display_label <- function(reason) {

  dplyr::case_when(

    reason ==
      "Visa application process" ~
      "Institutions citing visa application process",

    reason ==
      "Potential problems at the port of entry" ~
      "Institutions citing potential problems at the port of entry",

    reason ==
      "Enroll in another country's institutions" ~
      "Institutions citing enrollment in another country",

    reason ==
      "Securing a job in the United States after their studies" ~
      "Institutions citing difficulty securing a US job after study",

    reason ==
      "Cost of tuition/fees at U.S. host institution" ~
      "Institutions citing cost of tuition and fees",

    reason ==
      "U.S. travel restrictions" ~
      "Institutions citing US travel restrictions",

    reason ==
      "Feeling unwelcome in the United States" ~
      "Institutions citing students feeling unwelcome",

    reason ==
      "Social and political environment in the United States" ~
      "Institutions citing US social and political environment",

    reason ==
      "Visa status while in the United States" ~
      "Institutions citing visa status while in the US",

    reason ==
      "Stay home and enroll in their own country's higher education institutions" ~
      "Institutions citing students staying home to enroll",

    TRUE ~
      paste0(
        "Institutions citing ",
        stringr::str_to_lower(
          reason
        )
      )
  )
}


ch2_barrier_top3_stats <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  ch2_barrier_top3,

  function(
      Reason,
      Value2015,
      Value2025,
      Change,
      StatID,
      ...
  ) {

    out <- metric_values(
      stat_id =
        StatID,

      section_id =
        "recruitment",

      section =
        "Recruitment and barriers (2015–2025)",

      measure =
        ch2_barrier_display_label(
          Reason
        ),

      first_value =
        Value2015,

      first_label =
        2015,

      last_value =
        Value2025,

      last_label =
        2025,

      value_type =
        "percent_value",

      change_type =
        "pp_percent"
    )


    # * = left-column value is 2015 rather than 2001.
    out$Earlier <- paste0(
      format_value(
        Value2015,
        "percent_value"
      ),
      "*"
    )


    out$Latest <- format_value(
      Value2025,
      "percent_value"
    )


    out
  }
)

CH2_TAB202_FIELD_FILES <- list(
  "Engineering" = ch2_tab202a,
  "Math & Computer Science" = ch2_tab202b,
  "Physical & Life Sciences" = ch2_tab202c,
  "Business and Management" = ch2_tab202d,
  "Education" = ch2_tab202e,
  "Fine/Applied Arts" = ch2_tab202f,
  "Health Professions" = ch2_tab202g,
  "Social Sciences" = ch2_tab202h
)


CH2_TAB202_PROPORTION_FIELDS <- c(
  "Engineering",
  "Math & Computer Science",
  "Physical & Life Sciences"
)


ch2_tab202_long <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  CH2_TAB202_FIELD_FILES,

  function(
      df,
      field_name
  ) {

    df %>%
      mutate(
        Year =
          year_number(.data$Year),

        across(
          -Year,
          numeric_clean
        )
      ) %>%
      pivot_longer(
        -Year,
        names_to = "Country",
        values_to = "Share"
      ) %>%
      filter(
        is.finite(.data$Share)
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        Share = if (
          field_name %in%
            CH2_TAB202_PROPORTION_FIELDS
        ) {
          .data$Share * 100
        } else {
          .data$Share
        },

        Field =
          field_name
      )
  }
)


ch2_tab202_changes <- ch2_tab202_long %>%
  group_by(
    .data$Country,
    .data$Field
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    .data$Year,
    .by_group = TRUE
  ) %>%
  filter(
    n() >= 2
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    FirstYear =
      first(.data$Year),

    LastYear =
      last(.data$Year),

    First =
      first(.data$Share),

    Last =
      last(.data$Share),

    Change =
      .data$Last -
      .data$First,

    .groups =
      "drop"
  )


ch2_tab202_example_metric <- function(
    country,
    field,
    stat_id,
    emphasis = FALSE
) {

  row <- ch2_tab202_changes %>%
    filter(
      .data$Country ==
        .env$country,

      .data$Field ==
        .env$field
    )


  if (
    nrow(row) != 1
  ) {
    return(
      NULL
    )
  }


  metric_values(
    stat_id = stat_id,
    section_id = "field_shift",
    section = "How the field mix is shifting",

    measure = paste0(
      country,
      " — ",
      tolower(field)
    ),

    first_value =
      row$First[[1]],

    first_label =
      row$FirstYear[[1]],

    last_value =
      row$Last[[1]],

    last_label =
      row$LastYear[[1]],

    value_type =
      "percent_value",

    change_type =
      "pp_percent",

    emphasis =
      emphasis
  )
}


ch2_grad_tvh_metric <- function(
    df,
    field,
    stat_id,
    emphasis = FALSE
) {

  tmp <- df %>%
    transmute(
      Year =
        year_number(.data$Year),

      Temporary =
        numeric_clean(
          .data$`Temporary visa holders`
        ),

      Domestic =
        numeric_clean(
          .data$`U.S. citizens and permanent residents`
        )
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Share =
        .data$Temporary /
        (
          .data$Temporary +
            .data$Domestic
        )
    ) %>%
    filter(
      is.finite(.data$Year),
      is.finite(.data$Share)
    )


  metric_series(
    stat_id = stat_id,
    section_id = "graduate_tvh",
    section =
      "Temporary-visa share of graduate enrollment",
    measure = field,
    df = tmp,
    column = "Share",
    value_type = "share",
    change_type = "pp_share",
    emphasis = emphasis
  )
}


ch2_tab204b_normalized <- ch2_tab204b %>%
  rename(
    `Social Science` = any_of(
      "Social Sciences"
    )
  )


ch2_doctorate_tvh_metric <- function(
    field,
    stat_id,
    display_name = field,
    emphasis = FALSE
) {

  if (
    !field %in%
      names(ch2_tab204a) ||
      !field %in%
        names(ch2_tab204b_normalized)
  ) {

    return(
      NULL
    )
  }


  tmp <- inner_join(

    ch2_tab204a %>%
      transmute(
        Year =
          year_number(.data$Year),

        Domestic =
          numeric_clean(
            .data[[field]]
          )
      ),

    ch2_tab204b_normalized %>%
      transmute(
        Year =
          year_number(.data$Year),

        Temporary =
          numeric_clean(
            .data[[field]]
          )
      ),

    by = "Year"

  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Share =
        .data$Temporary /
        (
          .data$Temporary +
            .data$Domestic
        )
    ) %>%
    filter(
      is.finite(.data$Year),
      is.finite(.data$Share)
    )


  metric_series(
    stat_id = stat_id,
    section_id = "doctorate_tvh",
    section =
      "Temporary-visa share of research doctorates",
    measure = display_name,
    df = tmp,
    column = "Share",
    value_type = "share",
    change_type = "pp_share",
    emphasis = emphasis
  )
}

build_ch2_page <- function(
    page_data,
    page_number,
    total_pages,
    is_last_page
) {

  final_notes <- if (
    is_last_page
  ) {

    c(

      paste0(
        "\\* Marked rows use a baseline other than 2001, see note below. ",
        "ᴾ marks 2026 projected enrollment."
      ),

      paste0(
        "**Note:** Unless otherwise indicated rows compare 2001 and 2025.",
        "STEM-country rows compare 2010 and 2025. Recruitment and barrier rows compare 2015 and 2025.",
        "Arrow colors indicate direction of change only."
      ),

      paste0(
        "**Source:** Derived from the current report Figures and Tables: ",
        "Figures 2.01–2.08, Tables 2.01-2.02."
      )
    )

  } else {

    character()
  }


  build_infographic_table(
    data =
      page_data,

    id = paste0(
      "infographic_ch2_by_the_numbers_page_",
      sprintf(
        "%02d",
        page_number
      )
    ),

    chapter_number =
      2,

    title =
      "WHO COMES TO THE US TO STUDY?",

    subtitle =
      "The changing sources of America’s international STEM talent",

    column_labels = c(
      Earlier = "2001",
      Latest = "2025",
      Change = "Change"
    ),

    notes =
      final_notes,

    layout =
      INFOGRAPHIC_FIXED_LAYOUT,

    row_padding_px =
      INFOGRAPHIC_FIXED_LAYOUT$row_padding_px,

    nowrap_values =
      TRUE,

    trend_right_padding_px =
      5,

    show_header =
      FALSE
  )
}


ch2_exports <- export_paginated_infographic(
  data =
    ch2_selected,

  build_page =
    build_ch2_page,

  name =
    "infographic_ch2_by_the_numbers",

  rows_per_page =
    INFOGRAPHIC_ROWS_PER_PAGE,

  section_headers_per_page =
    CH2_SECTION_HEADERS_PER_PAGE
)
```

```{r infographic_ch3_by_the_numbers, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# ============================================================================
# CHAPTER 3: FROM EDUCATION TO THE WORKFORCE — BY THE NUMBERS
#
# Display convention:
#
#   MEASURE | 2000 | 2025 | CHANGE
#
#   - 2000 is the preferred historical comparison year.
#   - If 2000 is unavailable, use the usable observation closest to 2000
#     and show its actual year as a superscript.
#   - 2025 is the preferred latest comparison year.
#   - If the source ends before 2025, use the latest available observation
#     and show its actual year as a superscript.
#
# Degree-to-work averages:
#
#   OVERALL
#     Source: INF3-02
#     NSCG custom tabulation of relationship between field of highest degree
#     and occupational field.
#
#     Weighted average =
#
#       all bachelor's + master's + doctorate STEM-degree holders
#       working in S&E occupations
#       ---------------------------------------------------------
#       all employed bachelor's + master's + doctorate
#       STEM-degree holders
#
#   US-BORN / FOREIGN-BORN
#     Source: INF3-01
#     NCSES Table 6-4.
#
#     Weighted average =
#
#       all bachelor's + master's + doctorate graduates working
#       in S&E OR S&E-related occupations
#       ---------------------------------------------------------
#       all employed bachelor's + master's + doctorate graduates
#
#     This exactly preserves the definition used for FIG304a / FIG304b.
#
# H-1B:
#   - Top-10 employer concentration uses its longitudinal source through 2025.
#   - Individual employers compare 2017 with 2025.
#   - Display the two largest risers and two largest fallers.
#
# Editorial:
#   - No immigrant-founder or AI-company snapshot material.
#   - No snapshot rows.
#   - Exactly 32 statistics are displayed by default.
#
# Layout:
#   - 32 body rows permitted.
#   - 5 section headers permitted.
#   - Same shared typography / sizing as Chapters 1 and 2.
#   - No chapter title or subtitle is rendered.
# ============================================================================


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. INCLUDE / EXCLUDE CONTROLS
```
